findings.attack: The frozen main-start formula produces 24 primary starts and permits six retries for three eligible architectures, but the case catalog declares eight MODEL_IN_LOOP_FUTURE base cases across four families. Under the ordinary one-model-start-per-case interpretation, three architectures times eight cases times two repeats requires 48 primary starts before retries. The protocol does not define a family-bundling execution unit that reconciles this difference, and its formula also does not account for up to two Stage 2 component ablations. Therefore the 30-start cap is not yet demonstrably compatible with complete benchmark coverage.

findings.attack: The resource policy caps starts, wall time, storage, grader actions and maintained logical units, but it provides no absolute input-token or output-token ceiling. Token thresholds are only ratios to an unmeasured baseline. Monetary cost is explicitly UNKNOWN in the shadow scope, while operator effort, queue delay and future maintenance burden are not measured. This conflicts with the frozen rule that unknown cost yields EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT and prevents treating full Stage 2 affordability as established.

findings.attack: The catalog is stratified by component rather than by the architectural discriminants between workflow-language guards and a deterministic kernel. It contains one adversarial-gaming base case per component and two composite base cases per component, but no frozen mapping from W1/K1-specific failure modes to oracle classes, metrics or independent analysis units. Ten transformations per family and repeated runs do not by themselves establish independent discriminatory power. Consequently the benchmark may measure component conformance while failing to distinguish the claimed benefit of K1 over W1.
